title: Reimagining the retail pharmacy experience for today’s consumers
summary: As frontline healthcare destinations, retail pharmacies are well positioned to offer comprehensive patient care that goes beyond prescriptions
body_markdown:
*As frontline healthcare destinations, retail pharmacies are well positioned to offer comprehensive patient care that goes beyond prescriptions*


*By Naomi Duvall, vice president, consumer health*


According to the[Consumer Healthcare Products Association](https://www.chpa.org/sites/default/files/media/docs/2022-11/The-Power-of-OTCs-to-Provide-Consumer-Value.pdf) (CHPA), the average U.S. household spends more than $600 each year on over-the-counter (OTC) medications and other healthcare products.[McKinsey & Company](https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/consumer-packaged-goods/our-insights/future-of-wellness-trends) reports that consumers consistently prioritize overall wellness, with annual spending exceeding $500 billion and growing year over year.


Throughout my career, I've watched retail pharmacies become trusted destinations for treatment options that address patients’ health needs and complement their prescription medications. From the common cold to a minor injury, more than[80% of Americans](https://www.chpa.org/about-consumer-healthcare/infographics/81-adults-use-otc-medicines-first-response-minor-ailments) choose OTC products as their first response to everyday health concerns, according to CHPA. Patients are also seeking OTC products and wellness solutions at their local pharmacy before making an appointment with their primary care provider.


Simultaneously, technology has made health information more accessible than ever, empowering patients to learn about preventative care for medical conditions and recommended treatments with one quick online search. This has influenced consumers across generations to purchase products such as vitamins, supplements and other OTC items to support mobility, gut health, weight management, mental acuity and sleep.


As patients continue visiting their local pharmacy for healthcare products and wellness solutions, retail pharmacists must consider adapting their business models to keep pace. This includes assessing current trends shaping the retail pharmacy experience as patients shop in the aisles of their stores.


To help our pharmacy customers seize the opportunities created by consumers’ expectations of greater convenience, affordability and wellness support — and reinforce their position as community healthcare destinations — we are making strategic investments that strengthen our core distribution services.


**Enabling access and affordability**
Every day, through access to a broad, evolving portfolio of consumer health items, we help pharmacies differentiate their front-of-store offerings. As a result, they can curate a product mix tailored to the unique needs of their community, pairing OTC medications with personal care items. This includes everything from durable medical equipment (DME) and home medical supplies for aging residents to seasonal products that help patients stay healthy as the weather changes.


While the accessibility of front-end products drives foot traffic, we also help pharmacies consider the affordability of OTCs and wellness items as patients face rising healthcare costs and other economic pressures. Our private label brands,[LEADER™](https://myleader.com/) and[Major Rugby™](https://www.major-rugby.com/home) , allow pharmacies to increase access to[effective](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/generic-drugs/generic-drugs-questions-answers) but more affordable alternatives.


Additionally, with[more patients enrolling](https://www.kff.org/medicare/medicare-advantage-in-2026-enrollment-update-and-key-trends/) in Medicare Advantage programs that include OTC Benefit cards, pharmacists are well positioned to help patients navigate these plans and reduce out-of-pocket costs for essential consumer health products. We’ve partnered with the leading technology and software providers of these benefits to create easy platform access and a suite of tools that help pharmacists identify patient pools. By leveraging this platform, pharmacies unlock available benefits and generate additional front-end revenue while providing value and optimal care for their patients.


**Building the supply chain for the modern pharmacy**
As the healthcare industry evolves, we’re regularly evaluating our pharmaceutical distribution network to ensure pharmacies have timely, reliable access to the products they need. To help pharmacies stay ahead of changing patient needs across categories and continue expanding their front-end offerings, we opened our[Consumer Health Logistics Center (CHLC)](https://newsroom.cardinalhealth.com/2025-09-15-Cardinal-Health-Unveils-State-of-the-Art-Consumer-Health-Logistics-Center) .


A first-of-its-kind centralized replenishment hub, the CHLC represents a significant differentiator in how Cardinal Health supports pharmacies. It gives retail pharmacies access to one of the industry's broadest selections of consumer health products so their shelves remain stocked with the OTC medications and personal care items patients rely on. The facility's hub-and-spoke model also creates an agile, responsive supply chain that enhances our ability to deliver the right product to the right place at the right time, while providing supplier partners with efficient processes and accurate inventory management.


**Driving awareness and patient engagement**
Beyond product availability and affordability, an effective consumer health strategy promotes education and awareness. Pharmacies must think strategically about how marketing supports their overall front-end growth, and couple trusted in-store conversations with messaging across the advertising channels patients use every day.


We collaborate with our retail pharmacy customers to provide product assortment recommendations via monthly planogram merchandising packets, retail pricing updates and turnkey promotional programs. These programs help pharmacies keep their front of store current and aligned with industry trends so they can focus their time on patient care.


**Supporting pharmacies’ long-term growth**
Today’s retail pharmacies have significant opportunities to diversify revenue streams and retain patients by offering traditional dispensing alongside a comprehensive offering of consumer health and wellness-focused products that accompany foundational care.


At Cardinal Health, our commitment is clear: we will continue helping retail pharmacies build resilient businesses while strengthening the distribution services that deliver essential, in-demand healthcare products. Investments such as the CHLC — paired with our team’s deep pharmacy market expertise and dedication to expanding product categories based on industry trends — position us to continue providing the consumer health items that help retail pharmacies remain competitive and, most importantly, care for the patients and communities they serve.


*As vice president of Consumer Health at Cardinal Health, Naomi Duvall oversees a broad consumer health portfolio of products, programs and solutions. With nearly four decades of experience across the retail and healthcare continuum, she has led the evolution of our consumer health business into a high-growth, strategic differentiator. She and her team partner closely with suppliers and pharmacy customers to unlock profitability, optimize front-end retail and help pharmacies deepen their impact in the communities they serve.*
